time_plan.30m: Check whether the probability spike coincides with a macro shock headline (labor data, credit event) or is isolated market noise; verify Treasury futures (ZB/ZN) confirm the direction.
time_plan.1h: Compare Fed funds futures / SOFR curve repricing against the Polymarket move; a genuine signal should show 2026 easing being priced across the curve.
time_plan.2h: Reassess TLT vs 10y yield; if yields have not fallen, downgrade the thesis as a weak/noisy proxy.
time_plan.6h: Check for any Fed speaker or data release that explains the move; confirm whether move is persisting or mean-reverting.
time_plan.12h: Evaluate net TLT return vs the 700bps tradable threshold; almost certainly below it, log as directional-only research signal.

predictions.reasoning: A market pricing 11 Fed cuts (~275bps) in 2026 is an extreme easing/recession-crisis tail. A sharp upward move in that implied probability would signal expectations of aggressive Fed easing, which pushes front-end and long-end yields down and bond prices up. TLT is the cleanest liquid duration proxy for a dovish/emergency-cut regime.

predictions.reasoning: Eleven cuts in a year only happens in a crisis/recession scenario, which is typically equity-negative (growth collapse dominates). But aggressive easing is also a liquidity tailwind, so the sign is genuinely ambiguous over a 12h window — hence 'mixed' with low confidence. The proxy exposure to this specific tail is weak.

evidence_used: Market question implies 11 x 25bps = ~275bps of 2026 cuts, an extreme easing scenario far outside base-case Fed paths
Historical pattern: only recessions/financial crises produce that many cuts in a year
Standard macro linkage: aggressive Fed easing expectations -> lower yields (bonds up), weaker USD, risk-asset ambiguity
Mislabeled metadata (topic 'military_conflict', region 'unknown') is inconsistent with the actual monetary-policy question and was disregarded
uncertainty_notes: This is a deep-tail question; a probability 'spike' may still leave absolute odds tiny and carry little information
Direction of equities is genuinely ambiguous: crisis (down) vs liquidity (up)
Prediction markets on Fed policy are noisy and thin; move may not reflect leaked information
A 700bps 12h move in liquid ETFs is extremely unlikely absent a systemic shock, so predictions are unlikely to be 'tradable'

llm_justification.summary: The market asks about an extreme 11-cut (~275bps) easing path in 2026, which realistically only occurs in a recession or financial-crisis scenario. A sharp rise in its implied probability would most cleanly imply expectations of aggressive Fed easing: long-duration Treasuries (TLT) up on falling yields, with equities (SPY) ambiguous because crisis-driven downside competes with liquidity-driven upside. Both mappings are directional-only, low-confidence, and almost certainly below the 700bps tradable threshold over 12 hours.
key_assumptions: A probability move reflects genuine repricing of the Fed easing path rather than thin-market noise
Bond markets transmit the easing signal faster and more reliably than equities
No confounding, already-public catalyst fully explains the move
failure_modes: The move is noise in a thin tail market and reverses within hours
The information is already public (e.g., a data print) so assets have already repriced
TLT/SPY are weak proxies for this specific extreme scenario and fail to move meaningfully
Equity direction inverts if easing is read as bullish liquidity rather than recession
Magnitudes fall far short of 700bps, making both signals non-tradable
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
